issues.detail: The Hebrew phrase 'הַדָּמִין יִתְעֲבֵד וּבַיְתֵהּ נְוָלִי יִשְׁתַּוֵּה' means 'shall be cut in pieces, and their houses shall be made a dunghill' (i.e., the offender and his house). The Chinese renders only '必將他扔進烈火的糞堆中' ('will throw him into the fiery dung heap'), which conflates the two punishments: it omits the dismemberment ('cut in pieces') and misplaces the 'dunghill' as a fiery place of execution rather than the destruction of the house. This changes the factual content of the decree.

The Hebrew 'וּבַיְתֵהּ נְוָלִי יִשְׁתַּוֵּה' ('and his house shall be made a dunghill') is entirely omitted; the Chinese only mentions throwing the person into a fiery dung heap, losing the separate punishment on the house.
